To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) a plant DNA-viruses induces stromule formation in epidermal cells of its host plants, (ii) the heat shock cognate protein cpHSC70 is a major component of these stromules, (iii) cpHSC70 interacts with the viral MP and (iv) cpHSC 70 is involved in chloroplast maintenance and viral movement.
the induction of stromule biogenesis by a DNA-viruses is a novel phenomenon in plants and suggests a novel intra and intercellular trafficking route for macromolecular complexes.
AbMV induces stromule formation, and that the stromules contain the chaperone protein cpHSC70.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification and functional characterization of the role of stromules and their components in plant-virus interactions.
the role of cpHSC-70 and stromules in intra- and/or intercellular trafficking during AbMV-infection of its host plant.
a novel role of stromules as an intercellular transport system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
AbMV infection leads to the induction of stromules in which the viral MP is transported to neighboring cells, and that this is dependent on the presence of the host protein cpHSC70.
the interaction of AbMV with cpHSC70 is relevant for virus movement, and that this interaction is mediated via stromules, which are induced by the infection.
AbMV induces a remodulation in the host cell to support its own movement and replication.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
stromules are dynamic membrane protrusions of plastids that can be utilized by a DNA-viral MP to facilitate the movement process.
the induction of stromule networks by AbMV infection suggests a novel intra and intercellular trafficking route for macromolecules.
the induction of a cpHSC701-oligomeric stromule network by a plant DNA virus may be a strategy to facilitate virus movement and/or replication.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the interaction of AbMV MP with cpHSC70 and the subsequent formation of a stromule network is a prerequisite for the virus to spread systemically.
stromules are a novel route for intercellular trafficking in plants.
stromules might be a previously unknown trafficking route within the cell, and that they may be involved in virus movement.
